thread.title: Stocks Slip At Open, Then Bounce As Disney Rumbles, Snap Spikes

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stocks Slip At Open, Then Bounce As Disney Rumbles, Snap Spikes
text:
Stocks opened to modest declines, but quickly improved into mixed trade Wednesday, as global markets recovered and U.S. stocks felt for direction.
X The   average opened down 0.4%, but quickly reversed into a fractional gain. The Nasdaq Composite pared its opening loss to 0.3%, as Apple ( AAPL ) and Facebook ( FB ) both fell more than 1%. The S&P 500 eased its initial decline to less than 0.1%.
Market volatility — as measured by the Cboe Market Volatility Index , commonly called the VIX — spiked Monday and then again Tuesday before pulling back and ending sharply lower. Volatility is not necessarily a negative, it just means both gains and losses can evaporate quickly, making the market more unpredictable than usual. In the current setting, premarket gains tell an investor little about where the market may end the day.
Leading benchmarks across Asia were mixed Wednesday, with Tokyo's Nikkei 225 rebounding 0.2% while China's markets continued to carve deep losses. Trade in Europe gained strength in the afternoon session, with London's FTSE 100 up 1.1%, the DAX in Frankfurt trading 1% higher and the CAC-40 in Paris rising 0.8%.
Commodities generally showed moderate losses as the dollar rose vs. the euro and notched further declines against the yen. Bonds edged up, trimming the 10-year yield two basis points to 2.78%.
The economic calendar for Wednesday is light, showing only the Energy Information Administration's weekly oil inventories report at 10:30 a.m. ET, and the Federal Reserve's December Consumer Credit data due at 3 p.m. ET.
Speaking in Frankfurt, Germany, early Wednesday, Dallas Federal Reserve President Robert Kaplan described the U.S. market's recent volatility as a healthy correction, and contended that the recent acceleration in wage growth would not necessarily lead to a faster pace in the Fed's rate hike scheme.
New York Federal Reserve Bank President William Dudley was scheduled to speak at 8:30 a.m. ET, and Charles Evans of the Chicago Fed was scheduled for comments at 11:15 a.m.
Dow Stocks: Disney Climbs, United Tech, GE Lead; Snap Rockets Two-thirds of the Dow Jones names moved higher in the first 15 minutes of trade. Walt Disney ( DIS ) took the index's strongest opening gain, up more than 1% after its fiscal first-quarter earnings and revenue cleared analyst targets by a wide mark. Revenue from the entertainment giant's media networks was flat during the quarter, but revenue from theme parks and resorts surged 13% .
The stock closed Wednesday about 7% below a 113.29 buy point in a nine-month, cup-with-handle base .
Disney's early gain was rapidly overtaken as United Technologies ( UTX ) , General Electric ( GE ) and Boeing ( BA ) all advanced more than 1%.
Snap ( SNAP ) scored a 29% opening gain. The Snapchat parent reported a 13-cent loss per share vs. views for a 16-cent loss. It also clobbered analyst targets on its revenue line and added 11 million daily active users during the fourth quarter — three million more than consensus forecasts.
Snap shares have slogged along deep in an 11-month consolidation. The stock ended Tuesday 25% off an August low, and 17% below its March 2017 IPO price.
Wynn Resorts ( WYNN ) bolted 8% higher after the company announced founder, Chairman and Chief Executive Steve Wynn would step down and be replaced immediately by board director Matthew Maddox, both at the Wynn Resorts parent and at its high-profit Wynn Macau unit in China. Wynn Macau's shares had dropped 17% following news reports of sexual misconduct by CEO Wynn. JP Morgan also upgraded the stock Wednesday, to overweight, from neutral.
Akamai Technologies ( AKAM ) was up 6% after its quarterly reports. Shares traded just below a 69.66 buy point in a year-long cup-with-handle base .
Stock posting heavy losses on earnings news included BlackBox ( BBOX ), down 18%, Macom Technology Solutions ( MTSI ), with an 28% slide, and Chipotle Mexican Grill ( CMG ), which toppled 10%.
Among IBD 50 stocks, Viper Energy ( VNOM ) jumped out to an early lead, up 3.5% after reporting its fourth-quarter results late Tuesday.
